description:
Château de la Caze was built in 1490 by François Alamand as a wedding gift for his niece Soubeyrane. Although its architecture has the appearance of a medieval castle, its defensive elements are purely decorative — it was never more than a "vanity castle," without a strategic site or any real offensive or defensive character, built instead for comfort, well-being and appearance. It was listed as a historic monument in 1936 and registered on the historic monuments inventory in 1988.

Today its 16 rooms are split between the château (10 rooms) and the separate annex, "La Maison Martine" (6 rooms).

The château's deliberately decorative medieval styling, built at a time when genuine defensive fortresses were still common in the region, distinguishes la Caze from estates whose battlements and towers once served real military purposes.

The 1936 historic-monument listing, followed by formal inventory registration in 1988, gives la Caze two separate layers of French heritage protection spanning more than five decades.

The presence of a genuine, separate annex building — 6 of the 16 rooms — means more than a third of the property's room inventory sits outside the 1490 château itself.

The château's position directly on the Tarn river, within the Gorges du Tarn between limestone cliffs and forest, gives guests staying at la Caze one of the more dramatic natural settings among the France collection's château-hotels.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** At the heart of the Gorges du Tarn, beside the river, between limestone cliffs and forest.

**Rooms & rates:** 16 rooms — 10 in the 15th-century château, 6 in the separate "La Maison Martine" annex; from about €150 per night.

**On-site:** Spa, gym, private beach, helipad, restaurant.

**Good to know:** The château's architecture imitates a defensive medieval castle but never was one — built in 1490 as a "vanity castle" for comfort and appearance; 6 of the 16 rooms are in the separate annex, not the historic building.

**Combine with:** Sainte-Énimie (10 min), canoeing the Gorges du Tarn.
